The place I was originally planning to go to was full, so I looked around to see where I could go and saw that there was a new place so I decided to go. It's on the second floor of the building. I almost went into the hakama on the first floor by mistake;;

It seems like they sell about four types of pies as main dishes, and I ordered and tried ice cream and spinach pie. It seemed like there was a set time for new pies to be available, and if you took what was on display and ordered it, it would be warmed up and served to you.

The pie was not a sweet pie, but rather a quiche-like one. It consisted of ingredients (meat, cheese, etc.) that could be used as a meal replacement, and was soft, salty, and delicious.

I ordered ice cream as a main dish, and it seemed to be vanilla ice cream topped with two kinds of frozen berries, oil, salt, and pepper. I've had ice cream with the same toppings in the past that were very delicious, but it didn't have the same taste and strangely it felt like the taste of the toppings didn't go well with the ice cream, but overall it was delicious.

There are not many seats, but there are a few 4-person seats and many 2-person seats.
The chair was a bit uncomfortable to sit on for a long time.

Overall, it was clean and comfortable and it was nice to be able to enjoy delicious food. It would be nice to pack the pies and heat them up one at a time at home!

reviews.text:
I don't really like Starbucks, but I stop by every now and then when I'm curious about a new menu item I've seen in passing. I recently passed by and wanted to try the double espresso cream latte that I saw on the banner ad outside the store, so I skipped coffee at home this morning and stopped by this Reserve store.

When I entered the store, it seemed like it was a Reserve store, so the gold color was used appropriately and it exuded luxury. It was not divided into multiple floors, but was spacious on the first floor and the floor height was slightly high, so it had a good sense of openness, making it feel like it had an American feel.

In addition, the font for the English letters Hawaii used in the banner advertisement for Hawaii Kau Coffee, which seems to be on promotion recently, has a Hawaiian feel to it, giving me an exotic feeling that I have somehow entered a Starbucks store in Hawaii.

When I approached the counter and couldn't find the double espresso cream latte I had in mind, I inquired. The menu was a New Year promotional menu, but from today onwards, a female salesperson who seemed to be in charge and with a barista vibe told me that the promotional drinks had been changed to drinks with strawberries as the main drink. I had a moment of mental breakdown.

When I scanned the menu, it seemed like a coffee made with Blonde Espresso, a type of Starbucks coffee that I often brew with Nespresso at home, was on promotion, so I inquired about Blonde Espresso. I heard it had acidity and a light feel, so I knew it was light, but I wondered if it had acidity, so I, who likes acidity, was curious, and wondered if the Blonde Espresso I taste at the store was different. I asked for an iced Blonde Americano.

After waiting a bit, the Ice Blonde Americano I ordered came out, but then I realized that I had forgotten to upgrade the size.

When I picked it up and took a bite, I instantly liked the refreshing acidity and thought it was real. However, it wasn't as delicate or had a lingering aftertaste like at good roasters in Hapjeong, but the taste wasn't bland and the refreshing acidity was just good. I feel like this is the first time I've had coffee that made me smile at Starbucks.

Looking at the label on the cup, I don't know if it's real, but it says 3 shots, so I guess that's why it wasn't bland.

I stopped by to try the double espresso cream latte, which is a new year promotional menu item that I was curious about overall, but I heard that the promotional menu has changed from today, so I tried the Blonde Americano with ice instead. Surprisingly, it had a good refreshing acidity and wasn't too bland, so it was good. The store is also a reserve store, so it exudes luxury and is comfortable. The coffee taste alone is somewhere between okay and delicious, but the atmosphere of the store was good, so if you think about enjoying it in the store, I think you'll be satisfied. It's delicious...

Altdeep Dosan Tea Lounge offers a variety of unique tea menus, including milk tea, cream tea, tea cocktails, and tea-based desserts.

The cafe is located on the second floor of the building, so it's hard to see from the street unless you look for the sign. I visited on a Thursday afternoon and it was relatively quiet. The inside of the tea lounge is quite spacious and seats about 30 people.

I tried a few menu items and they were all not too sweet (which is exactly what I like) and each had a really unique taste.

Menu ordered:
Dosan Signature Purple Milk Tea (₩8,000) • 9.5/10
The subtle scent of lavender and vanilla combine to create a soft milk tea taste, with a hint of pineapple scent at the end. The sweet cream on top was also a nice addition to the flavor of the drink. This is a drink I really like.

Dosan Signature Black Cream (₩8,500) • 8.5/10
First, there is a strong coffee aroma, followed by a fragrant black tea aroma. The sweet yet salty cream topping was also very delicious.

Dosan Summer Citrus Milk Tea (₩7,500) • 9/10
This is a sweet milk tea with a refreshing citrus scent. The thinly sliced ​​orange garnish also goes well with the drink. It's perfect as a cool summer drink.

Signature Pudding Plate (₩12,500) • 10/10
The texture of the pudding is close to panna cotta, but a little creamier. The scent of hojicha and oolong tea is subtle. The sweet and crunchy crumbles and dried figs were also really delicious. This is a dessert where all the ingredients come together in one bite to give you a fantastic taste.

If you are near Dosan Park, I highly recommend you visit.

reviews.author: Sunghoon Kim
reviews.text:
If you have a lot of money, there is no cocktail bar like this. First of all, this store charges a cover charge of 10,000 won per person. As soon as I entered and sat down, I spent 10,000 won. Also, this is a place where smoking the cigars sold here takes place very naturally, so it is not recommended if you have an aversion to smoking.

The overall interior of the building is modeled after a cask used for whiskey maturation. It brings out the scent as if you were drinking alcohol from an oak barrel.

There are a lot of very expensive high-end whiskeys and a large quantity of limited-edition casks in stock. Even Haram, who is crazy about malt, will definitely have a shot that he has never tried. Of course, you'll be worried about your wallet.

Cocktails are also top-notch. In fact, it is not easy to rate cocktails because each bar has a different recipe and the standards of the person who makes it are all different. Nevertheless, I would like to give it a high rating.

To give a brief example, I ordered Saint-Germain Tonic (Photo 5). Crushed ice and ice with hibiscus tea base were divided into two glasses and served in half. When I told her that my taste was sherry whiskey, as well as Saint-Germain, they added additional flute essence. I experienced the magic of refreshing and sweet Saint-Germain Tonic mixing with hibiscus tea base over time and transforming into a unique drink.

The non-alcoholic cocktail (photo 3) was also good. It was a tea-based cocktail made with Earl Gray, several types of essence, cream, and milk mixed together and topped with chocolate powder as a garnish. The sweet, refreshing, and soft taste was excellent.

Lastly, all the glasses here were expensive products. The water glass provided as standard was also Riedel, so that's all.

I saw that snacks were not good as a basic snack, so try ordering raisin snacks with sherry whiskey. There is nothing that suits you better than this.
